  • ILL ³He target: helium bag and ³He leak rate 2026-10-02IllTargetHe3

    Air ¹⁴N comes from the 30 cm beam path, so a He flight tube fixes it; a balloon around the target does not help and floods the mylar cell. Bare 12 µm mylar loses ~22 L of ³He per cycle; a 1 bar cell with a 12 µm PET + 6–7 µm Al-foil skin cuts that >1000× for +3 % scattering. The foil sits outside the beam, Al is the right metal, and the scattering is set by the Micromegas entrance and the air.

  • How much charge does the gamma flash deliver? Two independent measurements 2026-08-09NTOFMicromegasGamma flashDAQ

Gain cannot fix it and the millisecond dead time follows from it.

MX174

  • det3 X neighbour asymmetry: an audit 2026-10-23DetectorCrosstalk

    CLOSED 2026-10-23, cause not identified. Fresh-eyes summary of the study. Every June board carries a smooth, two-signed, X-only field that moves charge from neighbour n−1 to n+1, sized by the cloud width alone. Electronics, copies, linear coupling, Y→X transfer, charging and gap conduction are excluded. 2026-10-22: the print film of the resistive strips measures 761 µm (not 780): if it is the production print, strip registration cannot make the field and the sim overstates the strips. 2026-10-23: no pillar lattice in the data either, and tracks cannot scan a pad. Fingerprint, exclusions, what is left.

  • MX17 response simulation: where it stands (2026-10-18) 2026-10-18SimulationMicromegasGarfield

    The MX17 Micromegas response simulation against det3 cosmics: amplitude and inclined strip extent now match (26.5 mm drift column, bG 0.45); the inclined-Y peak strip and the neighbour timing still disagree, and an inter-strip coupling closes part of the latter. What was fixed, what is open, and ideas to close it.

  • MX17 response simulation, animated 2026-10-12SimulationAnimation

    One muon through the whole simulation chain (Geant4 → Magboltz drift → Garfield avalanche and ions → resistive induction → DREAM → FEU → wft), which code does each part, and how its pulse compares with the real det3 average. Toggle the ion signal to see the T14 rise-time problem. Also: what runs per event (Geant4 + sampling) versus what Garfield/Magboltz computed once.

  • MX17 response simulation: state of play (Oct 2026) 2026-10-12SimulationT14

    The Geant4 → Garfield → induction → DREAM chain vs det3 cosmics: charge ×1.6 low, gain slope ×1.5 shallow, pulses too slow. An independent toy clears the code; the shaper is confirmed 180 ns, so the ion signal must be ≈ 5× suppressed, with no mechanism found.

  • Track passport: tracking and calorimetry on every track 2026-10-15X17MicromegasCalorimetryGeant4

    A pedagogical demonstrator: what the MX17 stack (Micromegas TPC, SiPM wall, plastic, liquid) measures about one particle, from the physics to Geant4 to 15,000 real n_TOF beam tracks: gas dE/dx to 16-22 %, electron energy to 0.9 MeV, two-particle and origin tags.

  • Scintillator calorimetry: muon-calibrated wall and plastic vs beam electrons and Geant4 2026-10-14X17ScintillatorsCalorimetryGeant4

    Calibrated once on cosmic muons, the SiPM wall and three of four plastic bars describe the beam electrons at Geant4's scale to ~5 %, stable to <1 %; bar C1 reads 15 % high and the PMTs sag 3-8 % at high rate.

  • Calorimetry feasibility: what the stack can measure 2026-10-08X17ScintillatorsCalibrationGeant4

    Plastic scale 3-24 % low at the muon (fixed), liquids threshold-limited, MM dE/dx and the soft-leg energy discriminant both killed (+5-8 % against IPC).
